headline: Airbnb launches AI travel agent in H1 2027
summary: The company aims to build a custom-designed AI experience that goes beyond traditional chatbots, offering a personalized interface with maps, photos, and comparisons.
details: Airbnb has announced its AI travel agent will launch in the first half of 2027, moving beyond previous teasers. The company's CEO, Brian Chesky, believes traditional chatbots are not ideal for travel planning, which he describes as an aspirational and enjoyable process.

Chesky emphasized that people enjoy researching trips and comparing options, often with travel companions. He stated that general-purpose AI agents are not suited for this, leading Airbnb to develop its own specialized agent.

Airbnb's AI agent will feature a personalized interface designed specifically for travel. Instead of just text responses, it will utilize a library of travel-specific components like maps, photos, and calendars, composing them in real-time to match user needs.

The agent is expected to feel like 'generative UI,' offering the 'right interface at the right time' for each user's unique travel requirements. This approach leverages Airbnb's nearly 20 years of experience in connecting hosts and guests.

Beyond booking, the AI agent will assist travelers throughout their trip, handling tasks such as changing reservations, resolving payment issues, processing refunds, rebooking, and providing 24-hour safety support.
The company anticipates the agent will eventually extend its capabilities to include services and experiences, areas that have become a greater focus for Airbnb following a recent redesign.

This announcement coincided with strong third-quarter earnings, which saw revenue grow 19% to $4.87 billion, surpassing Wall Street estimates. Airbnb also raised its 2026 revenue growth forecast to the high teens.

headline: Apple captures half of global smartphone revenue in Q3
summary: The tech giant's revenue share hit a new high, driven by strong sales of its latest iPhone models.
details: Apple achieved a record-breaking Q3 for global smartphone revenue, capturing 50% of the market according to Counterpoint Research.
This significant market share highlights Apple's dominant position in the premium smartphone segment.
The strong performance is attributed to the continued popularity of its iPhone lineup, particularly the newest releases.
While specific sales figures for individual models were not disclosed, the overall revenue surge indicates robust consumer demand for Apple's devices.
